definitions.explanation: A collective term for plant life in general, encompassing both grasses and trees. Often used in literary or poetic contexts to refer to nature or the natural world.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{草木|くさき}が{茂|しげ}っている。
examples.english: The plants in the garden are growing thick.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると{草木|くさき}が{一斉|いっせい}に{芽吹|めぶ}く。
examples.english: When spring comes, all the plants begin to sprout at once.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{冬|ふゆ}が{終|お}わり、{山|やま}の{草木|くさき}が{色|いろ}づき{始|はじ}めると、{村|むら}の{人々|ひとびと}はようやく{暖|あたた}かい{季節|きせつ}の{訪|おとず}れを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: When the long winter ends and the mountain vegetation begins to take on color, the villagers finally feel the arrival of the warm season.

notes:
USAGE:
{草木|くさき} literally combines {草|くさ} (grass) and {木|き} (tree) to mean plant life collectively. It carries a slightly literary or poetic tone compared to simply saying {植物|しょくぶつ} (plants).

The fixed expression {草木|くさき}も{眠|ねむ}る{丑三|うしみ}つ{時|どき} refers to the dead of night (around 2-3 AM), literally "the hour when even the plants sleep."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {草木|くさき}が{茂|しげ}る (vegetation grows thick)
- {草木|くさき}が{枯|か}れる (plants wither)
- {草木|くさき}が{芽吹|めぶ}く (plants sprout)
- {草木|くさき}が{生|お}い{茂|しげ}る (vegetation grows lush)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {植物|しょくぶつ}: plants (scientific, neutral term)
- {緑|みどり}: greenery (visual emphasis on the color)
